unit.sep: Classify exact quantities,model multiplicative inverses and verify a numerical decision.
unit.careers: Illustrative quantity planning,measurement and mathematical communication;no professional certification.
unit.content: Classification of numbers; Reciprocal of numbers
unit.phenomenon: A fictional class supply label calls every odd count prime and tries to undo division with an additive opposite.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Exact versusdisplayednumbers,signedfraction inverses,reciprocal tables,actual device records and portion planning.
unit.drivingQuestion: How do we use real numbers in day-to-day activities?
unit.coreCompetencies:
Communication and Collaboration: the learner discusses with peers to identify and categorise whole numbers as odd, even, prime, composite, rational, and irrational.
Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner uses the reciprocal of real numbers to work out mathematical tasks.
Digital Literacy: the learner works out the reciprocal of real numbers from calculators and other digital devices.
unit.values:
Unity: the learner discusses in a group and categorises real numbers as rational and irrational numbers.
Responsibility: the learner takes care of calculators and mathematical tables when working out the reciprocal of real numbers.
unit.pcis: Life Skills (self-esteem): the learner participates in the discussion on the concepts of rational and irrational numbers.

sections.title: 4. Plan and communicate a checked decision
sections.prompt: For the CRN10 supply/portion case, use multiplication by a reciprocal to find the number of full portions. Give units, the no-spill assumption and a reverse product check. Write two or three sentences of advice intended for a classmate that link this checked result or a correct classification to a concrete useful decision; include why0 cannot be a divisor. This final advice is written independently; do not consult or present to peers during assessment.
sections.exemplar: (7/2)L÷(7/8)L per portion=(7/2)×(8/7)=4full portions. Check4×7/8L=7/2L=3½L, assuming exact amounts and no spills. Example written advice: plan4full portions under those assumptions rather than guessing with an additive opposite. Use nonzero portion sizes because0 has no reciprocal. Accept varied specific correct classification/reciprocal advice tied to evidence, not a copied slogan; no unobserved delivery claim.
